paper_metadata.title: Variational quantum eigensolver with linear depth problem-inspired ansatz for solving portfolio optimization in finance

summary: The paper proposes two linear‑depth Dicke‑state ansätze (CCC and CC) for VQE portfolio optimization and evaluates them in simulation up to 20 qubits and on a superconducting quantum computer using a hybrid distributed computing scheme representing up to 55 logical qubits. Hardware experiments execute fragmented circuits on 3–6 qubit devices and demonstrate optimization convergence but do not show a runtime or solution-quality advantage over classical portfolio optimization methods.

experiments.description: Variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) portfolio optimization using the CCC ansatz, evaluated in noise-free simulation across varying asset counts, confidence levels, budgets, and asset orderings.

algorithm.variant: VQE with linear-depth problem-inspired Dicke-state CCC ansatz
algorithm.parameter_initialization: random seed 1231 for parameters; asset pools initialized with random seeds starting from 1000

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 1 qubit per asset; Dicke-state subspace encodes fixed-budget binary selection with Hamming weight k
problem_formulation.objective_function: min_x q x^T A x - mu^T x subject to 1^T x = k (budget constraint); CVaR used as objective estimator in VQE
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: hard constraint via Dicke-state ansatz; CVaR local cost function
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: diagonal Hamiltonian corresponding to q' z^T A' z - mu'^T z under the hard-constraint formulation

problem_instance.description: Binary integer portfolio optimization with mean-variance analysis

dataset_specification.description: synthetic/benchmark financial data generated with qiskit_finance.data_providers; 20 random asset pools

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: asset data generated from qiskit_finance.data_providers; no further preprocessing reported
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 20 independent asset-pool seeds; average time consumption, average optimal-solution probability, and average feasible-solution probability reported across configurations

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: asset pools generated with qiskit_finance.data_providers; asset ordering varied (original, reversed, shifted, random)
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: average probabilities and time consumption computed over repeated random seeds; feasible solution defined as expectation no more than 0.75 times optimal

speedup_claims.caveats: No classical baseline algorithm is reported; only comparisons among quantum ansatze (CCC, CC, HE) are shown.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: linear two-qubit gate depth; O(nk) parameters/gates

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: unknown; simulations only up to 20 qubits
limiting_factors: no comparison against strong classical portfolio optimizers

notes: Hardware is a simulator because the paper states these are numerical simulations performed by pyQPanda; no QPU used in this experiment.
Authors compare ansatz variants but do not demonstrate quantum advantage over classical portfolio optimization methods.
